title: Forked integration case runners never run the leak check, and a framework escape buffer leaks per thread
summary: parallel_case_runner.h runs every case in a forked child that ends with _exit(), so LeakSanitizer never runs and ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1 sanitizer runs of the scheduler and other suites report no leaks whatever happens. With an explicit __lsan_do_recoverable_leak_check() after each scheduler case, the only remaining report is in indigo_libs: indigo_xml_escape_b() keeps a thread-local long_escape_buffer that is never freed when a handler queue thread ends (seen through indigo_save_property() in repeat_retry_and_failures, 1183 bytes). Next: free the buffer at thread end or use a caller-owned buffer (framework change, needs owner approval), then run the leak check in the case runner child before _exit().
evidence: indigo_test/integration/parallel_case_runner.h _exit(runner->child(...)); indigo_libs/indigo_xml.c indigo_xml_escape_b(); per-case leak check experiment recorded in the task verification.md.
